label: new_skill

expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: Order is "Peer-reviewed journal articles" (1–5), then "Peer-reviewed conference paper" (6), then "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed" (7), then "Research organization and agency reports" (8–10).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Preprint: "*Why it's here:* it's the closest match to your exact sub-question. *Watch for:* it hasn't been peer reviewed". World Bank: "*Why it's here:* a strong design with high school students. *Watch for:* it's a working paper". Pew pair: "*Why these two are here:*... *Watch for:* they're surveys".

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.
expectations.evidence: "Six of these meet your peer-review requirement: these five plus the conference paper below."

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: No scores, tiers or rating levels appear. Labels such as "Peer-reviewed article" and "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed" name the type of source, not a rating.

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count.
expectations.evidence: Every link and DOI checks out. 10.1073/pnas.2422633122, 10.1111/bjet.13544, arxiv.org/abs/2409.09047 and both Pew URLs were fetched. 10.1186/s40561-025-00385-2, 10.1007/s10639-026-13924-2, 10.3390/soc15010006, 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.1502 and 10.1596/1813-9450-11125 appear in the DOIS ON OPENED PAGES list.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: Only one question mark is addressed to the user: "Which one surprised you most, and why?" The line "ask me how I know..." is an instruction, not a question.
